verifications.claim: A SSA Continuing Disability Review (CDR) is a periodic evaluation of the medical condition to determine if the person is still disabled and eligible for benefits.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Social Security Administration (SSA) is required to periodically check to make sure beneficiaries still have a disabling condition'; R2: 'we must evaluate your impairment(s) from time to time to determine if you are still eligible for payments based on disability'; R4: 'Social Security periodically reviews your medical impairment(s) to determine if you continue to have a disabling condition'; R5: 'The law requires that Social Security review your case from time to time to verify that you still have a disability'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly define CDR as a periodic review of medical condition to check ongoing disability and eligibility.

verifications.claim: SSA Continuing Disability Reviews occur every 6–18 months if improvement is expected.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Your first review could be as soon as six months after your disability began if Social Security expects your condition to improve'; R3: 'Medical improvement expected (MIE) – Reviews occur every 6 to 18 months'; R5: 'Expected, we'll normally review your medical condition within six to 18 months after our decision'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state 6-18 months for cases where medical improvement is expected.

verifications.claim: SSA Continuing Disability Reviews occur every 3–7 years if improvement is not expected.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Medical improvement not expected (MINE) – Reviews occur every 5 to 7 years'; R4: 'if you have a medical condition that is not expected to improve, we will still review your case, once every five to seven years'; R5: 'Not expected, we'll normally review your medical condition about every seven years'; R1: 'at least every seven years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify 5-7 years or 7 years for 'not expected' (MINE), but 3 years is for 'possible' improvement (MIP); claim incorrectly includes 3 years for 'not expected'.

verifications.claim: The SSA sends a letter and either the Form SSA-455 (Disability Update Report) or Form SSA-454 (Continuing Disability Review Report) during the CDR process.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'they will send you a letter... and a Continuing Disability Review Report or a Disability Update Report'; R4: 'using the SSA-454 (Continuing Disability Review Report) or SSA-455 (Disability Update Report) form'; R5: 'Medical Continuing Disability Review Report (SSA-454)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm letter and exact form names/numbers (SSA-455 Disability Update Report, SSA-454 CDR Report).

verifications.claim: Under the Medical Improvement Review Standard (MIRS), the SSA must determine if there has been medical improvement related to the ability to work.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'in medical reviews the medical improvement review standard will apply'; R1: 'decide if your condition has improved and if they think you are able to return to work'
verifications.reasoning: R2 explicitly names 'medical improvement review standard'; R1 ties it to improvement and ability to work.

verifications.claim: Names of doctors, medical records from the last 12 months, prescriptions, and information on any work done are what to provide for a CDR.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'names of your providers... medical records for any medications... all tests and treatments... Work activity'; R2: 'develop a complete medical history of at least the preceding 12 months'
verifications.reasoning: Sources list exactly these items: provider names, recent medical records/medications/tests, work activity.

verifications.claim: If the forms are not returned within 30 days, benefits may be stopped.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'You have 30 days to complete and return the forms and records... If you don’t respond, your benefits may stop'
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states the 30-day deadline and consequence of benefits stopping.

verifications.claim: If the SSA determines benefits should stop, the recipient has the right to appeal that decision.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'you have the right to appeal'; R2: 'give you an opportunity to appeal'; R3: 'You have the right to appeal'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm the right to appeal if benefits are stopped.
